claim: ATP-dependent chromatin remodelling proteins share ATPase domains that are adapted to regulate protein–DNA interactions.
source: ATP-dependent chromatin remodelling proteins represent a diverse family of proteins that share ATPase domains that are adapted to regulate protein–DNA interactions.
evidence: This is a general statement about chromatin remodeling proteins that draws from established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: The structure of Saccharomyces cerevisiae Chd1 protein engaged with nucleosomes in the presence of ADP-beryllium fluoride has been determined.
source: Here, we present structures of the Saccharomyces cerevisiae Chd1 protein engaged with nucleosomes in the presence of the transition state mimic ADP-beryllium fluoride.
evidence: The manuscript presents structural data obtained through cryo-EM experiments.

claim: The path of DNA strands through the ATPase domains indicates the presence of contacts conserved with single strand translocases.
source: The path of DNA strands through the ATPase domains indicates the presence of contacts conserved with single strand translocases and additional contacts with both strands that are unique to Snf2 related proteins.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis and comparison with known translocase structures.

claim: The path of DNA strands through the ATPase domains indicates additional contacts with both strands that are unique to Snf2 related proteins.
source: The path of DNA strands through the ATPase domains indicates the presence of contacts conserved with single strand translocases and additional contacts with both strands that are unique to Snf2 related proteins.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis and comparison with Snf2-related proteins.

claim: Two turns of linker DNA are prised off the surface of the histone octamer as a result of Chd1 binding.
source: Two turns of linker DNA are prised off the surface of the histone octamer as a result of Chd1 binding, and both the histone H3 tail and ubiquitin conjugated to lysine 120 are re-orientated towards the unravelled DNA.
evidence: This is directly observed in the structural data presented.

claim: Both the histone H3 tail and ubiquitin conjugated to lysine 120 are re-orientated towards the unravelled DNA upon Chd1 binding.
source: Two turns of linker DNA are prised off the surface of the histone octamer as a result of Chd1 binding, and both the histone H3 tail and ubiquitin conjugated to lysine 120 are re-orientated towards the unravelled DNA.
evidence: This is directly observed in the structural data presented.

claim: Changes to nucleosome structure can alter the way in which histone epitopes are presented.
source: This indicates how changes to nucleosome structure can alter the way in which histone epitopes are presented.
evidence: This is inferred from the observed repositioning of histone tails and ubiquitin in the structure.

claim: The extended family of ATPases related to the yeast Snf2 protein acts to alter DNA-protein interactions.
source: The extended family of ATPases related to the yeast Snf2 protein acts to alter DNA-protein interactions (Flaus et al., 2006; Narlikar et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The Mot1 protein acts on complexes between the TATA box binding protein BP and DNA.
source: For example, while the Mot1 protein acts on complexes between the TATA box binding protein BP and DNA (Wollmann et al., 2011), the Snf2 protein carries out ATP-dependent nucleosome disruption (CoteCôté et al., 1994).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The Snf2 protein carries out ATP-dependent nucleosome disruption.
source: For example, while the Mot1 protein acts on complexes between the TATA box binding protein BP and DNA (Wollmann et al., 2011), the Snf2 protein carries out ATP-dependent nucleosome disruption (CoteCôté et al., 1994).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Paired ATPase domains rearrange during the ATP hydrolysis cycle to create a ratchet like motion along DNA in single base increments.
source: At the heart of all these proteins are paired domains capable of rearranging during the ATP hydrolysis cycle to create a ratchet like motion along DNA in single base increments (Clapier et al., 2017; Gu and Rice, 2010; Velankar et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The yeast Chd1 protein acts to organise nucleosomes over coding regions.
source: The yeast Chd1 protein is a member of this protein family and acts to organise nucleosomes over coding regions (Gkikopoulos et al., 2011; Ocampo et al., 2016; Pointner et al., 2012; Tran et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Chd1 interacts with elongation factors including the Spt4-Spt5 proteins, Paf1 and FACT.
source: Consistent with this, Chd1 is known to interact with elongation factors including the Spt4-Spt5 proteins, Paf1 and FACT (Kelley et al., 1999; Krogan et al., 2002; Simic et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The partially redundant functions of Chd1 and Isw1 in organising nucleosomes over coding regions are required to prevent histone exchange and non-coding transcription.
source: The partially redundant functions of Chd1 and Isw1 in organising nucleosomes over coding regions are in turn required to prevent histone exchange and non-coding transcription (Hennig et al., 2012; Radman-Livaja et al., 2012; Smolle et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The distribution of many histone modifications is ordered with respect to promoters.
source: In addition to the positioning of nucleosomes, the distribution of many histone modifications is ordered with respect to promoters (Liu et al., 2005; Mayer et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Histone H3 K4 methylation is frequently observed at promoters.
source: For example, histone H3 K4 methylation is frequently observed at promoters, while histone H3 K79 and K36 trimethylation are detected in coding regions (Kizer et al., 2005; Li et al., 2003; Pokholok et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Histone H3 K79 and K36 trimethylation are detected in coding regions.
source: For example, histone H3 K4 methylation is frequently observed at promoters, while histone H3 K79 and K36 trimethylation are detected in coding regions (Kizer et al., 2005; Li et al., 2003; Pokholok et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Histone H2B is ubiquitinylated within coding regions.
source: Histone H2B is also observed to be ubiquitinylated within coding regions (Fleming et al., 2008; Xiao et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Ubiquitinylation of histone H2B at lysine 123 in budding yeast is dependent on the E2 ligase Rad6.
source: Ubiquitinylation of histone H2B at lysine 123 in budding yeast, H2B K120 (H2BK120ub) in mammals, is dependent on the E2 ligase Rad6 (Robzyk et al., 2000) and the E3 ligase Bre1 (Hwang et al., 2003; Wood et al., 2003) and removed by the deubiquitinases Ubp8 and Ubp10 (Bonnet et al., 2014; Schulze et al., 2011; Wyce et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Ubiquitinylation of histone H2B at lysine 123 in budding yeast is dependent on the E3 ligase Bre1.
source: Ubiquitinylation of histone H2B at lysine 123 in budding yeast, H2B K120 (H2BK120ub) in mammals, is dependent on the E2 ligase Rad6 (Robzyk et al., 2000) and the E3 ligase Bre1 (Hwang et al., 2003; Wood et al., 2003) and removed by the deubiquitinases Ubp8 and Ubp10 (Bonnet et al., 2014; Schulze et al., 2011; Wyce et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: H2B ubiquitinylation is removed by the deubiquitinases Ubp8 and Ubp10.
source: Ubiquitinylation of histone H2B at lysine 123 in budding yeast, H2B K120 (H2BK120ub) in mammals, is dependent on the E2 ligase Rad6 (Robzyk et al., 2000) and the E3 ligase Bre1 (Hwang et al., 2003; Wood et al., 2003) and removed by the deubiquitinases Ubp8 and Ubp10 (Bonnet et al., 2014; Schulze et al., 2011; Wyce et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: A specific reader of H2BK120ub has not been identified.
source: A specific reader of H2BK120ub has not been identified.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: H2BK120ub assists the histone chaperone FACT in enabling transcription through chromatin.
source: However, H2BK120ub does assist the histone chaperone FACT in enabling transcription through chromatin (Pavri et al., 2006), and has been found to be required for methylation of histone H3 K4 and K79 (Sun and Allis, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: H2BK120ub is required for methylation of histone H3 K4 and K79.
source: However, H2BK120ub does assist the histone chaperone FACT in enabling transcription through chromatin (Pavri et al., 2006), and has been found to be required for methylation of histone H3 K4 and K79 (Sun and Allis, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Mutation of the writer enzymes or K120 itself disrupts nucleosome organisation.
source: An intriguing aspect of H2BK120ub is that while mutation of the writer enzymes or K120 itself disrupts nucleosome organisation, deletion of the deubiquitinylases increases chromatin organisation (Batta et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Deletion of the deubiquitinylases increases chromatin organisation.
source: An intriguing aspect of H2BK120ub is that while mutation of the writer enzymes or K120 itself disrupts nucleosome organisation, deletion of the deubiquitinylases increases chromatin organisation (Batta et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: H2BK120ub increases nucleosome repositioning mediated by Chd1.
source: Consistent with this H2BK120ub increases nucleosome repositioning mediated by Chd1 (Levendosky et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Yeast Chd1 functions predominantly as a single polypeptide.
source: Yeast Chd1 serves as a useful paradigm in that it functions predominantly as a single polypeptide.
evidence: This is established knowledge about yeast Chd1.

claim: The catalytic core of Chd1 has been crystallised in association with the adjacent tandem chromodomains.
source: In addition, the catalytic core of the enzyme has been crystallised in association with the adjacent tandem chromodomains (Hauk et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The C-terminal region of Chd1 includes SANT and SLIDE domains that comprise the DNA binding domain.
source: Similarly the C-terminal region of the protein has been crystalized revealing that this region includes SANT and SLIDE domains that comprise the DNA binding domain (DNABD) (Ryan et al., 2011; Sharma et al., 2011) and are also present in ISWI proteins (Grüne et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: SANT and SLIDE domains are present in ISWI proteins.
source: Similarly the C-terminal region of the protein has been crystalized revealing that this region includes SANT and SLIDE domains that comprise the DNA binding domain (DNABD) (Ryan et al., 2011; Sharma et al., 2011) and are also present in ISWI proteins (Grüne et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Chd1 enzyme engages nucleosomes in a conformation in which the SANT and SLIDE domains bind linker DNA, while the ATPase domains engage DNA at super helical location (SHL) 2.
source: Chd1 enzyme engages nucleosomes in a conformation in which the SANT and SLIDE domains bind linker DNA, while the ATPase domains engage DNA at super helical location (SHL) 2 (Nodelman et al., 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Higher resolution structures of Chd1, Snf2 and INO80 show that the ATPase domains make contacts with DNA via residues that are conserved in ancestral single-stranded ATPases and some unique to Snf2-related ATPases.
source: Higher resolution structures of Chd1 (Farnung et al., 2017), Snf2 (Liu et al., 2017) and INO80 (Ayala et al., 2018; Eustermann et al., 2018) show that the ATPase domains make contacts with DNA via residues that are conserved in ancestral single-stranded ATPases and some unique to Snf2-related ATPases.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The binding of the Chd1 DNABD unravels two turns of DNA from the surface of nucleosomes in a nucleotide-stimulated reaction.
source: The binding of the Chd1 DNABD unravels two turns of DNA from the surface of nucleosomes in a nucleotide-stimulated reaction (Farnung et al., 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Nucleosomes were prepared in which histone H3 K36 was alkylated to mimic trimethylation.
source: As Chd1 functions on transcribed genes, it is of interest to understand the interplay between Chd1 and histone modifications observed in coding region chromatin. As a result, nucleosomes were prepared in which histone H3 K36 was alkylated to mimic trimethylation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) and H2B cross-linked to ubiquitin (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods used, with reference to supporting figures.

claim: H2B was cross-linked to ubiquitin in the prepared nucleosomes.
source: As Chd1 functions on transcribed genes, it is of interest to understand the interplay between Chd1 and histone modifications observed in coding region chromatin. As a result, nucleosomes were prepared in which histone H3 K36 was alkylated to mimic trimethylation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) and H2B cross-linked to ubiquitin (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods used, with reference to supporting figures.

claim: Conditions were established to favour binding of a single Chd1 to modified nucleosomes that included an asymmetric linker DNA extension of 14 bp in the presence of ADP-BeF.
source: Conditions were established to favour binding of a single Chd1 to modified nucleosomes that included an asymmetric linker DNA extension of 14 bp (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B) in the presence of ADP-BeF.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental conditions used.

claim: 2D classification of 893000 particles revealed 16 classes in which nucleosomes with the Chd1 molecule attached could be identified.
source: 2D classification of some 893000 particles revealed 16 classes in which nucleosomes with the Chd1 molecule attached could be identified (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is a description of the data processing results.

claim: Initial 3D classification resulted in five related classes.
source: Initial 3D classification resulted in five related classes (Figure 1—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is a description of the data processing results.

claim: A map with an average resolution of 4.5 Å (FSC 0.143) was generated.
source: This resulted in the generation of a map with an average resolution of 4.5 Å (FSC 0.143) (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This is a description of the final structural resolution obtained.

claim: The resolution is highest in the region occupied by the nucleosome and ATPase lobes and lower resolution in the vicinity of the DNABD and ubiquitin peptides.
source: The resolution varies within the map, with resolution highest in the region occupied by the nucleosome and ATPase lobes and lower resolution in the vicinity of the DNABD and ubiquitin peptides (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This is a description of the local resolution variation in the structure.

claim: The nucleosome particles exhibited a preferred orientation, which may limit the resolution.
source: The nucleosome particles exhibited a preferred orientation, which may limit the resolution (Figure 1—figure supplement 4C).
evidence: This is an observation from the data processing with speculation about its effect on resolution.

claim: The overall organisation of Chd1 is similar to that observed previously by cryo EM and directed cross-linking.
source: The overall organisation of Chd1 is similar to that observed previously by cryo EM (Farnung et al., 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017) and directed cross-linking (Nodelman et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a comparison with previous structural studies.

claim: The ATPase domains are bound at the SHL-2 location.
source: The ATPase domains are bound at the SHL-2 location.
evidence: This is directly observed in the structure.

claim: The bound site is in closest proximity to SANT-SLIDE domain bound linker DNA in physical space, but distal on the unwrapped linear DNA sequence.
source: Of the two SHL2 locations within nucleosomes, the bound site is in closest proximity to SANT-SLIDE domain bound linker DNA in physical space, but distal on the unwrapped linear DNA sequence (Figure 1).
evidence: This is an observation from the structure.

claim: Chd1 predominantly contacts the nucleosome via contacts with DNA, via the DNABD in the linker and ATPase lobes at SHL2.
source: Chd1 predominantly contacts the nucleosome via contacts with DNA, via the DNABD in the linker and ATPase lobes at SHL2; contacts with histones are limited to the histone H3 and H4 N-terminal regions discussed below.
evidence: This is an observation from the structure.

claim: Contacts with histones are limited to the histone H3 and H4 N-terminal regions.
source: Chd1 predominantly contacts the nucleosome via contacts with DNA, via the DNABD in the linker and ATPase lobes at SHL2; contacts with histones are limited to the histone H3 and H4 N-terminal regions discussed below.
evidence: This is an observation from the structure.

claim: Chd1 binding results in nucleotide-dependent unwrapping of nucleosomal DNA resulting from the interaction of the DNABD with linker DNA.
source: We previously showed that Chd1 binding results in nucleotide-dependent unwrapping of nucleosomal DNA resulting from the interaction of the DNABD with linker DNA (Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Precisely two turns of nucleosomal DNA are unravelled in the current structure.
source: The higher resolution of the current structure shows that precisely two turns of nucleosomal DNA are unravelled (Figure 1).
evidence: This is directly observed in the structure.

claim: The extent of DNA unwrapping observed when Chd1 is bound to nucleosomes flanked by a 14 base pair linker DNA is identical to that observed when Chd1 is bound to the opposite surface of the 601 nucleosome positioning sequence with a 63 base pair linker.
source: The extent of DNA unwrapping observed here when Chd1 is bound to nucleosomes flanked by a 14 base pair linker DNA is identical to that observed when Chd1 is bound to the opposite surface of the 601 nucleosome positioning sequence with a 63 base pair linker (Farnung et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a comparison with a previous structure.

claim: The extent of unwrapping is dominated by the properties of Chd1 rather than the affinity of DNA for the octamer.
source: As the interaction of histones with the two sides of the 601 positioning sequence differ quite dramatically (Chua et al., 2012; Hall et al., 2009; Levendosky et al., 2016; Ngo et al., 2015), this suggests that the extent of unwrapping is dominated by the properties of Chd1 rather than the affinity of DNA for the octamer.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of structures and knowledge about the 601 sequence.

claim: The path of unwrapped DNA is oriented away from the plane of the wrapped DNA gyre and is kinked at the location where contacts are made with the SANT-SLIDE domains.
source: The path of this unwrapped DNA is oriented away from the plane of the wrapped DNA gyre and is kinked at the location where contacts are made with the SANT-SLIDE domains (Figure 1).
evidence: This is directly observed in the structure.

claim: No additional changes in the organisation of DNA on Chd1 bound nucleosomes are detected at this resolution other than DNA unwrapping.
source: Other than DNA unwrapping, we do not detect additional changes in the organisation of DNA on Chd1 bound nucleosomes at this resolution.
evidence: This is a statement about what was not observed in the structure.

claim: The orientation of the DNABD is critical in determining the extent of DNA unwrapping.
source: The orientation of the DNABD is critical in determining the extent of DNA unwrapping.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural observations.

claim: The only contacts detected between the DNABD and the remainder of Chd1 are contacts with the chromodomains.
source: The only contacts detected between the DNABD and the remainder of Chd1 are contacts with the chromodomains (Figure 2 contact I and II).
evidence: This is directly observed in the structure.

claim: The first contact between DNABD and chromodomains is the interaction between K329 of chromodomain II and D1201 P1202 in the SLIDE component of the DNABD.
source: The first of these is the interaction between K329 of chromodomain II and D1201 P1202 in the SLIDE component of the DNABD and has been observed previously (Farnung et al., 2017; Nodelman et al., 2017) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is directly observed in the structure and has been reported previously.

claim: The second contact is between S344 and K345 in the linker helix between chromodomain II and ATPase lobe I with the SANT component of the DNA binding domain at D1033-D1038.
source: The second contact is between S344 and K345 in the linker helix between chromodomain II and ATPase lobe I with the SANT component of the DNA binding domain at D1033-D1038 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is directly observed in the structure.

claim: The residues contacted in the SANT and SLIDE domains are most highly conserved in Chd1 proteins.
source: Given that chromodomains are present in Chd1 enzymes but not ISWI and Snf2 remodellers, it makes sense that the residues contacted in the SANT and SLIDE domains are most highly conserved in Chd1 proteins (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B) (Hall et al., 2009; Meng et al., 2015; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).
evidence: This is based on sequence conservation analysis and citations to previous work.

claim: The chromodomains undergo an 18 degree rotation when compared to the orientation observed in the crystal structure of Chd1 in the open state.
source: This is indeed the case as the chromodomains undergo an 18 degree rotation when compared to the orientation observed in the crystal structure of Chd1 in the open state (Figure 3).
evidence: This is based on comparison with a previous crystal structure.

claim: Following repositioning, chromodomain I interacts with nucleosomal DNA at SHL1.
source: Following repositioning, chromodomain I interacts with nucleosomal DNA at SHL1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2) as observed previously (Farnung et al., 2017; Nodelman et al., 2017).
evidence: This is directly observed in the structure and has been reported previously.

claim: Coincident with repositioning of the chromodomains, ATPase lobe II is repositioned closer to lobe I.
source: Coincident with repositioning of the chromodomains, ATPase lobe II is repositioned closer to lobe I.
evidence: This is directly observed in the structure.

claim: Repositioning of ATPase lobe II results in residues including those contributing to the conserved Walker box motifs being brought into an arrangement compatible with ATP catalysis.
source: This results in residues including those contributing to the conserved Walker box motifs (K407 and R804, R807) being brought into an arrangement compatible with ATP catalysis.
evidence: This is directly observed in the structure and inferred from knowledge of ATP catalysis.

claim: Density for ADP-BeF within the pocket formed by conserved residues from ATPase domains I and II is well defined.
source: Density for ADP-BeF within the pocket formed by conserved residues from ATPase domains I and II is well defined (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is directly observed in the electron density map.

claim: The repositioning of ATPase lobe II enables contacts to be made with nucleosomal DNA, the histone H4 tail and the histone H3 alpha one helix.
source: The repositioning of ATPase lobe II enables contacts to be made with nucleosomal DNA (see below), the histone H4 tail and the histone H3 alpha one helix (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is directly observed in the structure.

claim: The contacts with nucleosomal DNA, the histone H4 tail and the histone H3 alpha one helix are the only direct contacts with histone components of the nucleosome.
source: The repositioning of ATPase lobe II enables contacts to be made with nucleosomal DNA (see below), the histone H4 tail and the histone H3 alpha one helix (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).These are the only direct contacts with histone components of the nucleosome.
evidence: This is directly observed in the structure.

claim: The contact with the H4 tails is conserved in mtISWI and Snf2.
source: The contact with the H4 tails is conserved in mtISWI and Snf2 (Liu et al., 2017; Yan et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on comparison with other structures.

claim: D729 and E669 are conserved across all classes of remodelling enzyme but D725 is not as well conserved in Snf2-related enzymes.
source: D729 and E669 are conserved across all classes of remodelling enzyme but D725 is not as well conserved in Snf2-related enzymes (Figure 2—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This is based on sequence conservation analysis.

claim: The conservation of the H4 tail contact in Chd1 enzymes is consistent with the H4 tail playing an important role in regulating Chd1 activity.
source: The conservation of this contact in Chd1 enzymes is consistent with the H4 tail playing an important role in regulating Chd1 activity; deletion or mutation of the H4 tail has been shown to reduce nucleosome sliding and ATPase activity (Ferreira et al., 2007).
evidence: This is inferred from conservation analysis and supported by citation to previous functional studies.

claim: Deletion or mutation of the H4 tail has been shown to reduce nucleosome sliding and ATPase activity.
source: The conservation of this contact in Chd1 enzymes is consistent with the H4 tail playing an important role in regulating Chd1 activity; deletion or mutation of the H4 tail has been shown to reduce nucleosome sliding and ATPase activity (Ferreira et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The additional helices that make up the protrusion 2 region of ATPase lobe two in Chd1 are conserved in chromatin remodeling ATPases, but not within all SF2 DNA translocases.
source: The additional helices that make up the protrusion 2 region of ATPase lobe two in Chd1 are conserved in chromatin remodeling ATPases, but not within all SF2 DNA translocases.
evidence: This is based on sequence conservation analysis and knowledge of protein families.

claim: Residues ranging from 632 to 647 pack against the alpha 1 helix of histone H3.
source: However, within the structure presented here residues ranging from 632 to 647 pack against the alpha 1 helix of histone H3.
evidence: This is directly observed in the structure.

claim: The two conserved residues K632 and K642 are located closer to H3 α1 D81 and E73.
source: In particular the two conserved residues K632 and K642 are located closer to H3 α1 D81 and E73 (Figure 2—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This is directly observed in the structure.

claim: Deletion of lobe two loop K632-K646 abolishes nucleosome sliding.
source: Deletion of this lobe two loop K632-K646 abolishes nucleosome sliding consistent with a role for this region in Chd1 action (Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is based on experimental data from a deletion mutant.

claim: The residues participating in the interaction between lobe two and H3 α1 are progressively less well conserved in ISWI and SNF2 related proteins.
source: The residues participating in the interaction are progressively less well conserved in ISWI and SNF2 related proteins (Figure 2—figure supplement 4C).
evidence: This is based on sequence conservation analysis.

claim: A loop from Phe1033 to Leu 1045 in an equivalent region of the yeast Snf2 protein is positioned such that a related contact with histone H3 could be made.
source: A loop from Phe1033 to Leu 1045 in an equivalent region of the yeast Snf2 protein is not assigned in the Snf2-nucleosome structure, but this region is positioned such that a related contact with histone H3 could be made.
evidence: This is speculative inference based on comparison with the Snf2 structure.

claim: A central event in driving conformational changes is likely to be the closure of the cleft between ATPase domains driven by ATP binding.
source: A central event is likely to be the closure of the cleft between ATPase domains driven by ATP binding (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is inferred from the structural observations.

claim: The 40 degree rotation of ATPase lobe II required to form the ATP binding pocket results in a positively charged surface being replaced by an acidic surface likely to repel chromodomain I.
source: The 40o rotation of ATPase lobe II required to form the ATP binding pocket results in a positively charged surface, observed to interact with an acidic surface on the long helix of chromodomain I (Figure 3A) (Hauk et al., 2010), being replaced by an acidic surface likely to repel chromodomain I (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is inferred from the structural observations and comparison with the open state.

claim: Closure of the ATPase domains is anticipated to drive nucleotide-dependent repositioning of the chromodomains.
source: As a result, closure of the ATPase domains is anticipated to drive nucleotide-dependent repositioning of the chromodomains.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural observations.

claim: The distance between engineered labels at V256C in chromodomain I and S524C in ATPase lobe1 is 4.4 nm in the open state.
source: The distance between engineered labels at V256C in chromodomain I and S524C in ATPase lobe1 is 4.4 nm in the open state, consistent with that observed in the crystal structure of the Chd1 chromoATPase domains (Hauk et al., 2010).
evidence: This is based on pulsed EPR measurements.

claim: In the presence of ADP-BeF a proportion of molecules adopt a new conformation with a distance of 5.6 nm.
source: In the presence of ADP-BeF the 4.4 nm distance predominates, but a shoulder is observed consistent with a proportion of molecules adopting a new conformation with a distance of 5.6 nm (Figure 4) which is similar to that observed in the ADP-BeF bound nucleosome by cryo-EM.
evidence: This is based on pulsed EPR measurements.

claim: ATP binding is a driving event for repositioning of the chromodomains.
source: This indicates that ATP binding is a driving event for repositioning of the chromodomains.
evidence: This is inferred from the EPR data showing nucleotide-dependent conformational change.

claim: The partial repositioning of the chromodomains observed in free Chd1 is likely to be stabilised by additional favourable interactions formed when this repositioning occurs within the context of nucleosome bound Chd1.
source: The partial repositioning of the chromodomains observed in free Chd1 is likely to be stabilised by additional favourable interactions formed when this repositioning occurs within the context of nucleosome bound Chd1.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural observations.

claim: The repositioning of the chromodomains acts as a lever to reposition the DNA binding domain.
source: The repositioning of the chromodomains in turn acts as a lever to reposition the DNA binding domain.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural connectivity.

claim: In the context of nucleosomes chromodomain repositioning results in nucleotide-dependent unwrapping of two turns of nucleosomal DNA.
source: In the context of nucleosomes this results in nucleotide-dependent unwrapping of two turns of nucleosomal DNA (Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: With a linker length of 19 bp Chd1 can be modelled binding the linker between adjacent nucleosomes.
source: With a linker length of 19 bp Chd1 can be modelled binding the linker between adjacent nucleosomes (Figure 5).
evidence: This is based on molecular modeling.

claim: As the linker between nucleosomes is reduced, steric clashes become increasingly prohibitive.
source: However, as the linker between nucleosomes is reduced, steric clashes become increasingly prohibitive.
evidence: This is based on molecular modeling.

claim: The requirement for a 19 bp linker is likely to provide a limit below which engagement of the DNABD will be less stable.
source: The requirement for a 19 bp linker is likely to provide a limit below which engagement of the DNABD will be less stable.
evidence: This is inferred from the modeling results.

claim: Seven base pairs of DNA make contact with the DNABD on a mononucleosome with a free DNA linker.
source: As this lower limit is set by clashes between the DNABD and the adjacent nucleosome, it is different from the length of linker required to occupy the DNA-binding surface of the SANT and SLIDE domains on a mononucleosome with a free DNA linker. In this latter case, seven base pairs of DNA make contact with the DNABD (Figure 1).
evidence: This is directly observed in the structure.

claim: The c19 bp separation below which access of the DNABD to linker becomes progressively more difficult resonates with the average inter-nucleosome spacing of 19 bp observed in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.

source: Density for ADP.BeF is observed in the nucleotide binding pocket, and the ATPase domains are repositioned to a closed conformation with conserved residues positioned for catalysis (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is directly observed in the structure.

claim: The ATPase domains are repositioned to a closed conformation with conserved residues positioned for catalysis.
source: Density for ADP.BeF is observed in the nucleotide binding pocket, and the ATPase domains are repositioned to a closed conformation with conserved residues positioned for catalysis (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is directly observed in the structure.

claim: The closure of the ATPase domains in the Chd1-nucleosome complex is connected to repositioning of the chromodomains, which in turn levers the DNABD position and allows DNA to gain access to the cleft between the ATPase domains.
source: The closure of the ATPase domains in the Chd1-nucleosome complex is connected to repositioning of the chromodomains, which in turn levers the DNABD position and allows DNA to gain access to the cleft between the ATPase domains.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural observations.

claim: The initial stages of remodelling by Chd1 are most effective on nucleosomes lacking exit DNA.
source: We nonetheless speculate that the initial stages of remodelling by Chd1 are most effective on nucleosomes lacking exit DNA.
evidence: This is speculative inference.

claim: The initial rate of Chd1 ATPase activity has been observed to be greater on nucleosomes lacking exit linker DNA.
source: Consistent with this the initial rate of Chd1 ATPase activity has been observed to be greater on nucleosomes lacking exit linker DNA (Nodelman et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Lack of linker in cells could arise in close packed nucleosomes and represent a suitable substrate for a nucleosome spacing enzyme.
source: In cells, lack of linker could arise in close packed nucleosomes and represent a suitable substrate for a nucleosome spacing enzyme.
evidence: This is speculative inference about the cellular context.

claim: The rapid action of Chd1 on close packed chromatin would generate new exit linker DNA which would then be available to be bound by the DNABD in the conformation observed by in the EM structures.
source: The rapid action of Chd1 on close packed chromatin would generate new exit linker DNA which would then be available to be bound by the DNABD in the conformation observed by in the EM structures.
evidence: This is speculative inference about the mechanism.

claim: Chd1 bound in the conformation shown in Figure 1 could be active but represent a state in which the DNABD is bound to exit rather than entry DNA.
source: In this case, Chd1 bound in the conformation shown in Figure 1, could be active but represent a state in which the DNABD is bound to exit rather than entry DNA.
evidence: This is speculative inference about the mechanism.

claim: The proposed mechanism requires that the Chd1 ATPase domains exhibit a preference for initial binding to nucleosomes on the side that initially lacks linker DNA.
source: However, it requires that the Chd1 ATPase domains exhibit a preference for initial binding to nucleosomes on the side that initially lacks linker DNA.
evidence: This is a logical requirement of the proposed mechanism.

claim: In the case of ISWI enzymes the initial and subsequent translocation events have been observed to differ.
source: The basis for this is not clear, but in the case of ISWI enzymes the initial and subsequent translocation events have been observed to differ (Deindl et al., 2013), raising the possibility that they could be regulated independently.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The engagement of the DNABD with the new exit linker may provide an opportunity for large changes in enzyme conformation.
source: Following initial repositioning, the engagement of the DNABD with the new exit linker may provide an opportunity for large changes in enzyme conformation, perhaps related to those observed for SNF2H (Leonard and Narlikar, 2015) and enabling individual Chd1 molecules to switch between different sides of the nucleosome enabling bidirectional repositioning (Qiu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is speculative inference supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Both budding yeast Chd1 and human Chd2 are found to be enriched within coding regions.
source: Both budding yeast Chd1 and human Chd2 are found to be enriched within coding regions (de Dieuleveult et al., 2016; Gkikopoulos et al., 2011; Lee et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Histone H3 K36me3 is a hallmark of coding region nucleosomes.
source: Histone H3 K36me3 is a hallmark of coding region nucleosomes, so we prepared nucleosomes alkylated to mimic trimethylation at this position.
evidence: This is established knowledge about histone modifications.

claim: Alkylation of H3K36 modestly stimulates Chd1 activity.
source: Alkylation modestly stimulates Chd1 activity (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), raising the possibility that this modification is recognised by the enzyme, possibly via the chromodomains.
evidence: This is based on experimental data.

claim: Electron density for the histone H3 tail is observed to residue 26, indicating that H3K36 does not stably interact with the chromodomains or any other component of Chd1 in the structure.
source: However, we observe electron density for the histone H3 tail to residue 26, indicating that H3K36 does not stably interact with the chromodomains or any other component of Chd1 in the structure reported here.
evidence: This is directly observed in the structure.

claim: For H3K36 to interact with chromodomains, either the chromodomains would need to be repositioned, or the structure of the N-terminus of H3 reconfigured.
source: Furthermore, for this interaction to occur, either the chromodomains would need to be repositioned, or the structure of the N-terminus of H3 reconfigured for example by unfolding of the alpha–N helix (Elsässer et al., 2012; Liu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is inferred from the structural observations and supported by citations.

claim: The improved density for the H3 tail on the unwrapped side of the nucleosome is most likely to result from the interaction of the basic N-terminal region of the H3 tail with DNA.
source: The improved density for the H3 tail on the unwrapped side of the nucleosome is most likely to result from the interaction of the basic N-terminal region of the H3 tail, which is not resolved, with DNA.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural observations.

claim: In the fully wrapped state the H3 tail would need to follow a very different path in order to interact with DNA.
source: It is notable that in the fully wrapped state the H3 tail would need to follow a very different path in order to interact with DNA.
evidence: This is inferred from comparison with other structures.

claim: The trajectory of the H3 tail on the unwrapped side of the nucleosome is different to that observed in structures of intact nucleosomes.
source: Consistent with this the trajectory of the H3 tail on the unwrapped side of the nucleosome is different to that observed in structures of intact nucleosomes (Wilson et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on comparison with previous structures.

claim: Changes to DNA wrapping could affect the way in which histone tail epitopes are displayed.
source: This raises the possibility that changes to DNA wrapping could affect the way in which histone tail epitopes are displayed.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural observations.

claim: The tudor domain of PHF1 preferentially interacts with trimethylated H3K36 on partially unwrapped nucleosomes.
source: For example the tudor domain of PHF1 preferentially interacts with trimethylated H3K36 on partially unwrapped nucleosomes (Gibson et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The interaction of the PHD domains of Chd4 with DNA is inhibited by nucleosomal DNA.
source: The interaction of the PHD domains of Chd4 with DNA is also inhibited by nucleosomal DNA (Gatchalian et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: If Chd4 generates unwrapped structures similar to those observed with Chd1 the interaction of PHD domains would be enhanced.
source: As a result if Chd4 generates unwrapped structures similar to those observed with Chd1 the interaction of these domains would be enhanced.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural observations and previous functional data.

claim: The reconfiguration of the H3 tail by Chd1 has the potential to affect the interaction of histone reader, writer and eraser enzymes with the tail.
source: The reconfiguration of the H3 tail by Chd1 has the potential to affect the interaction of histone reader, writer and eraser enzymes with the tail and as a result the distribution of these modifications in chromatin.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural observations.

claim: Chd1 contributes to the establishment of boundaries between H3K4me3 and H3K36me3 at most transcribed genes.
source: Such effects have been observed, as Chd1 contributes to the establishment of boundaries between H3K4me3 and H3K36me3 at most transcribed genes (Lee et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: H2BK120ub is enriched in coding region chromatin.
source: H2BK120ub is also enriched in coding region chromatin, and directly stimulates Chd1 activity (Levendosky et al., 2016) (Figure 8—figure supplement 2) (Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature and experimental data.

claim: H2BK120ub directly stimulates Chd1 activity.
source: H2BK120ub is also enriched in coding region chromatin, and directly stimulates Chd1 activity (Levendosky et al., 2016) (Figure 8—figure supplement 2) (Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature and experimental data.

claim: H2BK120ub negatively affects the activity of some ISWI containing enzymes.
source: It has also been observed that H2BK120ub negatively affects the activity of some ISWI containing enzymes (Fierz et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: H2BK120Ub has the potential to regulate interplay between different chromatin remodeling enzymes.
source: As organisation of coding region nucleosomes involves these and other enzymes (Krietenstein et al., 2016; Ocampo et al., 2016; Parnell et al., 2015), H2BK120Ub has the potential to regulate interplay between different enzymes.
evidence: This is inferred from the functional data and supported by citations.

claim: Ubiquitin on the unwrapped side of the nucleosome is repositioned such that it interacts directly with DNA.
source: Ubiquitin on the unwrapped side of the nucleosome is repositioned such that it interacts directly with DNA.
evidence: This is directly observed in the structure.

claim: The repositioning of ubiquitin resulting from Chd1-directed DNA unwrapping could potentially affect interactions with the factors involved in the placing, removal or recognition of H2BK120ub.
source: As in the case of the H3 tail, the repositioning of the ubiquitin resulting from Chd1-directed DNA unwrapping could potentially affect interactions with the factors involved in the placing, removal or recognition of H2BK120ub.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural observations.

claim: H2BK120ub is greatly reduced in Chd1 mutants.
source: The most striking functional evidence for this interplay is that H2BK120ub is greatly reduced in Chd1 mutants (Lee et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: One possible explanation for the reduction of H2BK120ub in Chd1 mutants is that Chd1 sequesters ubiquitin in a conformation less accessible for removal.
source: One possible explanation for this effect is that Chd1 sequesters ubiquitin in a conformation less accessible for removal.
evidence: This is speculative inference from the functional data.

claim: The position of ubiquitin on the unwrapped side of Chd1 bound nucleosomes is incompatible with interaction with the SAGA DUB module.
source: Consistent with this, the position of ubiquitin on the unwrapped side of Chd1 bound nucleosomes is incompatible with interaction with the SAGA DUB module (Morgan et al., 2016).
evidence: This is inferred from comparison with the structure of the SAGA DUB module and supported by citation.

claim: The paradigm for trans regulation between histone modifications stems from the interplay between H2BK120ub and H3 K4 methylation.
source: Interestingly, the paradigm for trans regulation between histone modifications stems from the interplay between H2BK120ub and H3 K4 methylation (Sun and Allis, 2002), both of which are influenced by Chd1 binding.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Both H2BK120ub and H3 K4 methylation are influenced by Chd1 binding.
source: Interestingly, the paradigm for trans regulation between histone modifications stems from the interplay between H2BK120ub and H3 K4 methylation (Sun and Allis, 2002), both of which are influenced by Chd1 binding.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural and functional data.

claim: Chd1 is not required for H3K4me3.
source: While Chd1 is not required for H3K4me3 (Lee et al., 2012), it does influence the distribution of this histone modification (Lee et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Chd1 influences the distribution of H3K4me3.
source: While Chd1 is not required for H3K4me3 (Lee et al., 2012), it does influence the distribution of this histone modification (Lee et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: H2BK120ub has previously been observed to directly affect chromosome structure at the level of chromatin fibre formation.
source: H2BK120ub has previously been observed to directly affect chromosome structure at the level of chromatin fibre formation (Debelouchina et al., 2017; Fierz et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: H2BK120ub has a role at the level of nucleosomal DNA wrapping.
source: Our observations show a new role for H2BK120ub at the level of nucleosomal DNA wrapping.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural observations.

claim: The specific relocation of ubiquitin on the unravelled side of the nucleosome indicates this is a favourable interaction that stabilises DNA in the unwrapped state.
source: The specific relocation of ubiquitin on the unravelled side of the nucleosome, the local distortion of H2B at the site of attachment and the presence of lysine and arginine residues at the site of interaction with DNA all indicate this is a favourable interaction that stabilises DNA in the unwrapped state.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural observations.

claim: The outer turns of nucleosomal DNA rapidly associate and dissociate on millisecond time scales, with occupancy of the unwrapped state estimated at 10%.
source: The outer turns of nucleosomal DNA rapidly associate and dissociate on millisecond time scales, with occupancy of the unwrapped state estimated at 10% (Li et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The ubiquitin interaction would be anticipated to stabilise the transiently unwrapped state increasing its abundance.
source: The ubiquitin interaction we have observed would be anticipated to stabilise the transiently unwrapped state increasing its abundance.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural observations.

claim: It is unlikely that the unwrapped state predominates in the absence of Chd1 or other factors that promote unwrapping as the structure of isolated ubiquitinylated nucleosomes is unchanged.
source: It is however, unlikely that the unwrapped state predominates in the absence of Chd1 or other factors that promote unwrapping as the structure of isolated ubiquitinylated nucleosomes is unchanged (Machida et al., 2016).
evidence: This is inferred from comparison with previous structural data and supported by citation.

claim: Increased occupancy of the transiently unwrapped state would be anticipated to facilitate access to nucleosomal DNA.
source: Nonetheless, increased occupancy of the transiently unwrapped state would be anticipated to facilitate access to nucleosomal DNA.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural observations.

claim: Chromatin folding to form higher order structures is likely to be favoured by fully wrapped nucleosomes.
source: Chromatin folding to form higher order structures is likely to be favoured by fully wrapped nucleosomes, and so an increase in the proportion of unwrapped nucleosomes could potentially contribute to the effects of H2BK120ub on chromatin fibre formation (Fierz et al., 2011).
evidence: This is inferred from knowledge of chromatin structure and supported by citation.

claim: Many processes involving chromatin dynamics are linked to H2BK120ub including transcription, DNA repair and DNA replication.
source: Many other processes involving chromatin dynamics are linked to H2BK120ub including transcription (Bonnet et al., 2014), DNA repair (Moyal et al., 2011; Nakamura et al., 2011) and DNA replication (Lin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: A more stable unwrapped state could provide an explanation for the association of factors that lack recognised ubiquitin interaction domains, with ubiquitinylated chromatin.
source: A more stable unwrapped state could also provide an explanation for the association of factors that lack recognised ubiquitin interaction domains, with ubiquitinylated chromatin (Shema-Yaacoby et al., 2013).
evidence: This is inferred from the structural observations and supported by citation.

claim: H2BK120ub associating proteins include human Chd1, SWI/SNF complex, pol II and the elongation factors NELF and DISF.
source: Interestingly, H2BK120ub associating proteins include human Chd1, SWI/SNF complex, pol II and the elongation factors NELF and DISF (Shema-Yaacoby et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The change in the position of ubiquitin has the potential to indirectly affect the way in which other factors interact with ubiquitinylated nucleosomes.
source: The change in the position of ubiquitin also has the potential to indirectly affect the way in which other factors interact with ubiquitinylated nucleosomes.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural observations.

claim: On the wrapped side of the nucleosome, ubiquitin is positioned such that it occludes access to the acidic patch.
source: On the wrapped side of the nucleosome, ubiquitin is positioned such that it occludes access to the acidic patch formed by the cleft between histones H2A and H2B.
evidence: This is directly observed in the structure.

claim: The acidic patch provides a surface via which many proteins interact with nucleosomes.
source: This provides a surface via which many proteins including LANA peptides (Barbera et al., 2006), RCC1 (Makde et al., 2010), Sir3 (Armache et al., 2011), PRC1 (McGinty et al., 2014) and the SAGA DUB module (Morgan et al., 2016) interact with nucleosomes.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The repositioning of ubiquitin away from the acidic patch on the unwrapped side of the nucleosome improves access to the acidic patch.
source: The repositioning of ubiquitin away from the acidic patch on the unwrapped side of the nucleosome improves access to the acidic patch.
evidence: This is directly observed in the structure.

claim: H2BK120ub may provide a means of regulating access to the acidic patch that is sensitive to changes in nucleosome structure.
source: In this way, H2BK120ub may provide a means of regulating access to the acidic patch that is sensitive to changes in nucleosome structure.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural observations.

claim: The repositioning of the H3 tail and ubiquitin were observed on Chd1-bound nucleosomes.
source: Although the repositioning of the H3 tail and ubiquitin were observed on Chd1-bound nucleosomes, the potential for reconfiguration of histone epitopes may be more general.
evidence: This is a statement about the observations in this study.

claim: The potential for reconfiguration of histone epitopes may be more general than just Chd1-bound nucleosomes.
source: Although the repositioning of the H3 tail and ubiquitin were observed on Chd1-bound nucleosomes, the potential for reconfiguration of histone epitopes may be more general.
evidence: This is inferred from the observations.

claim: All processes that generate local DNA unwrapping would be anticipated to result in similar repositioning of histone tail epitopes.
source: All processes that generate local DNA unwrapping would be anticipated to result in similar repositioning of histone tail epitopes.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural observations.

claim: Where combinations of modifications are recognised bivalently, the spatial alignment of epitopes will be important for recognition by coupled reader domains.
source: In particular, where combinations of modifications are recognised bivalently, the spatial alignment of epitopes will be important for recognition by coupled reader domains.
evidence: This is inferred from knowledge of how reader domains work.

claim: Reconfiguration of histone epitopes provides a means of tuning signalling via histone modifications to regions of transient histone dynamics.
source: This potentially provides a means of tuning signalling via histone modifications to regions of transient histone dynamics.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural observations.
